# 13. An interrupted `version` run resumes from its recorded inputs

Status: Proposed

## Context

- `version` rewrites the files it plans from (manifests, specs, changesets), then refreshes lockfiles. When the refresh fails (E208), a re-run plans from the half-written tree and is refused (E121). The docs name the gap: "a fresh command does not retain that plan" ([versioning](../architecture/versioning.md#idempotent-apply)).
- Release reruns need no recorded state because providers stay observable ([ADR 3](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md)); a `version` run's inputs are not observable after it has rewritten them.

## Decision

Before its first write, `version` records its inputs (`HEAD`, the working tree, the index, and the tags and flags planning reads) as a commit at `refs/worktree/callisto/checkpoint/version`, and deletes the ref when the run completes. A re-run while the ref exists plans from those inputs and reapplies idempotently. It first applies the plan in a scratch worktree of the checkpoint to learn what a finished run leaves, and refuses, writing nothing, unless every file the plan was derived from or writes is on disk as recorded or as that expected tree has it. The ref is per worktree, so a linked worktree has its own checkpoint. Discarding a run is a command, `callisto version --abort`: it puts back the files the run wrote that still hold its output, removes the files it created (never an ignored one), leaves and reports a file edited since, and keeps the checkpoint until nothing is left to put back.

## Options considered

- **Restore the written files when a step fails** — rejected: each review of #543 found another file state Git already restores correctly (lockfiles from an earlier ecosystem, binary files, symlinks, read-only files).
- **Re-plan from the versions at `HEAD`** — rejected: planning also reads dependency specs from disk, and a prototype resume dropped a dependent the first run had rewritten, exiting 0.

I found five defects the Change introduces, one more that applies only to persistent workspaces, and two lesser notes. I built the real binary and reproduced each in throwaway repos (scripts in /tmp/claude-501/lab). `cargo test -p callisto-cli --test version_resume_tests` passes (18/18). I did not run clippy, fmt or `just`.

I could not break the core of the design. The resume and abort paths I tried held up:
- an E208 abort restored the state byte for byte, and a late emit failure matched too
- an untracked changeset, staged-only plus unstaged edits, and a repeated abort came back identical
- an abort from a subdirectory, and `--dry-run --abort` (E276) behaved correctly
- a resumed run matched an uninterrupted one, including the `--emit-decision` and `--emit-preview` bytes
- an added package, a version edit in an unrelated package, a hand-edited changelog, and a post-interruption commit were all refused with E340
- I found no leftover scratch worktrees, temp index or refs after E208, E340, abort, dry-run or a successful resume

## Defects

### 1. `create_checkpoint` runs `git add -A` over the whole root, so unrelated state can fail every real `version` run, including a no-op one
- Where: `crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/checkpoint.rs:81-90`, called from `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs:232-236`. The checkpoint is created whenever `applying` is true, even when the plan writes nothing.
- Repro 1: `bash setup.sh n3`, then `echo secret > n3/crates/a/scratch.txt; chmod 000 n3/crates/a/scratch.txt`, then `callisto version`.
  - Observed: `E051 git add -A -- . failed ... unable to index file 'crates/a/scratch.txt'`.
  - `callisto --dry-run version` on the same repo succeeds.
  - The same happens with no pending changesets (`n1`).
- Repro 2: `git config core.safecrlf true; git config core.autocrlf input` plus an untracked file with mixed line endings. Result: `fatal: CRLF would be replaced by LF`, exit 1 (`n2`).
- Expected: `version` should not fail because of files it never reads or writes. Before this Change only specific paths were passed to `git add`.
- Performance: the temp index is built with `read-tree HEAD`, so it has no stat cache and `git add -A` rehashes every tracked file too. `git add -A` took 2.1 s on a fresh index versus 0.05 s on a copy of the real index (30k files, 120 MB). The same real `version` run took 3.0 s against 0.4 s for `--dry-run`. The cost scales with the tree, and `create_checkpoint` runs through `run_with_env`, which has the 60 s `LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` (`crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs:11`), so a very large tree would hit it.
- Fix:
  - Skip the checkpoint when the plan writes nothing.
  - Seed the temp index from a copy of the real index (`.git/index`) instead of `read-tree HEAD`; `add -A` on that copy still gives the working tree.
  - Or record only tracked files plus the plan's inputs and writes.

### 2. A user's `post-checkout` hook runs in the scratch worktree, and a failing hook blocks resume and `--abort`
- Where: `crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/checkpoint.rs:223-232` (`git worktree add`).
- Repro: `bash t_hook.sh`. After an E208 failure, install a `.git/hooks/post-checkout` that exits 1. Both `callisto version` and `callisto version --abort` fail with `E051 git worktree add --detach ... failed`.
  - The hook ran with cwd set to the scratch directory.
  - Each failure leaves a prunable registration (`.git/worktrees/tree`, `tree1`, ...). Nothing removes it, because `ResumeTree` is only built after `add_checkpoint_worktree` returns Ok.
- Expected: the scratch checkout is internal and should run no user code. The documented escape hatch (`--abort`) should not depend on the user's hooks.
- Fix: run the worktree add and the soft reset with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, and remove the registration when either step fails.

### 3. `--abort` writes plain text to stdout under `--format json`
- Where: `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs:69, 77, 109` use `emit_line`.
- Repro: `callisto --format json version --abort` prints `Discarded the interrupted ``version`` run.` on stdout and exits 0. The same happens with "No interrupted..." and the HEAD-moved message.
- Expected: stdout carries only the JSON document under `--format json`. The repo's `log_line(format, ..)` (`crates/callisto-cli/src/output.rs:69`) exists for this: it sends the line to stderr under json.
- Fix: use `log_line(global.format, ..)`, or emit a report.

### 4. `--abort` leaves the decision file the run emitted, while reporting "Discarded"
- Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:495-496`. The abort touches only the plan's written paths plus lockfiles, and the checkpoint records none of the `--emit-*` paths.
- Repro: `callisto version --emit-decision .callisto/release-decision.json --emit-preview crates` writes the decision, then the preview fails. `callisto version --abort` prints `Discarded the interrupted version run`, but `.callisto/release-decision.json` remains (`?? .callisto/` in status). If that file were tracked, it would stay modified.
- Expected: ADR 13 says abort "removes the files it created", and the user's state should match the pre-run state.
- Fix: record the emitted decision path in the checkpoint (a trailer) and restore or remove it on abort. Alternatively, make abort say it does not touch emitted files.

### 5. Abort reverts or removes lockfiles the plan does not write, contradicting VER-APPLY-20
- Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:495-512`. Line 505 treats every lockfile as "run output" without any comparison, so a lockfile edit made since the interruption is never classified as edited.
- Repro: after an E208 failure (`w2`), `echo '# user edit' >> Cargo.lock`, then `callisto version --abort`. It exits 0 and `Cargo.lock` is back to its recorded content, so the edit is lost. A lockfile the user created after the interruption (for example by running `npm install` themselves) is deleted the same way if it is not ignored.
- Expected: VER-APPLY-20 says "A file the plan does not write is never touched" and "leaves a file the user edited since".
- Fix: only restore or remove a lockfile when it is unchanged from what the run could have produced. If that is not knowable, report it as E342 instead of silently overwriting it. Otherwise, correct the spec.

### 6. On a persistent workspace the checkpoint can wedge the release PR action
- Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:437-439` (HEAD moved gives E340). `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh` never calls `--abort`. This applies only to reused runners; ADR 13 assumes ephemeral CI.
- Repro (`t_ci.sh`): an E208 run, then `git reset --hard; git clean -ffdx` (what a re-checkout does) plus a new commit on main, then `callisto version`. The tree is clean, yet it fails with E340 "HEAD moved". It stays wedged until someone runs `--abort`. `refs/worktree/*` survives the checkout.
- Fix: let the action handle E340 by running `callisto version --abort` and retrying. Or make a resume with a clean tree and a moved HEAD discard the checkpoint instead of refusing.

## Lesser notes
- `core.autocrlf=input` with a CRLF working file: abort restores LF bytes (`git restore -W` smudges nothing under `input`) and leaves the file showing ` M` in status, where the user's pre-run state was clean (`t_crlf.sh`). `autocrlf=true` is unaffected.
- `analyze_resume` runs `git ls-files --error-unmatch` through `is_staged` (`checkpoint.rs:117`). When a consumed changeset is absent, the runner echoes `error: pathspec '...' did not match any file(s) known to git` / `Did you forget to 'git add'?` to stderr during an otherwise successful abort or resume.

Also checked, no defect found:
- `analyze_resume` reads only the live workspace's manifests, so an unrelated package deleted between runs goes unnoticed; that is harmless, since a bumped or rewritten one is in `written` and caught.
- `--abort` with `--refresh-lockfiles` is accepted silently; the clap `conflicts_with_all` omits it.
- `files_at` and `untracked_files` read git output that is not `-z`, so non-ASCII changeset names are quoted. This matters only for the pre-mode retained-changeset check.

- Expected: stdout carries only the JSON document under `--format json`. The repo's `log_line(format, ..)` (`crates/callisto-cli/src/output.rs:69`) exists for this: it sends the line to stderr under json.
- Fix: use `log_line(global.format, ..)`, or emit a report.

### 4. `--abort` leaves the decision file the run emitted, while reporting "Discarded"
- Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:495-496`. The abort touches only the plan's written paths plus lockfiles, and the checkpoint records none of the `--emit-*` paths.
- Repro: `callisto version --emit-decision .callisto/release-decision.json --emit-preview crates` writes the decision, then the preview fails. `callisto version --abort` prints `Discarded the interrupted version run`, but `.callisto/release-decision.json` remains (`?? .callisto/` in status). If that file were tracked, it would stay modified.
- Expected: ADR 13 says abort "removes the files it created", and the user's state should match the pre-run state.
- Fix: record the emitted decision path in the checkpoint (a trailer) and restore or remove it on abort. Alternatively, make abort say it does not touch emitted files.

### 5. Abort reverts or removes lockfiles the plan does not write, contradicting VER-APPLY-20
- Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:495-512`. Line 505 treats every lockfile as "run output" without any comparison, so a lockfile edit made since the interruption is never classified as edited.
- Repro: after an E208 failure (`w2`), `echo '# user edit' >> Cargo.lock`, then `callisto version --abort`. It exits 0 and `Cargo.lock` is back to its recorded content, so the edit is lost. A lockfile the user created after the interruption (for example by running `npm install` themselves) is deleted the same way if it is not ignored.
- Expected: VER-APPLY-20 says "A file the plan does not write is never touched" and "leaves a file the user edited since".
- Fix: only restore or remove a lockfile when it is unchanged from what the run could have produced. If that is not knowable, report it as E342 instead of silently overwriting it. Otherwise, correct the spec.

### 6. On a persistent workspace the checkpoint can wedge the release PR action
- Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:437-439` (HEAD moved gives E340). `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh` never calls `--abort`. This applies only to reused runners; ADR 13 assumes ephemeral CI.
- Repro (`t_ci.sh`): an E208 run, then `git reset --hard; git clean -ffdx` (what a re-checkout does) plus a new commit on main, then `callisto version`. The tree is clean, yet it fails with E340 "HEAD moved". It stays wedged until someone runs `--abort`. `refs/worktree/*` survives the checkout.
- Fix: let the action handle E340 by running `callisto version --abort` and retrying. Or make a resume with a clean tree and a moved HEAD discard the checkpoint instead of refusing.

## Lesser notes
- `core.autocrlf=input` with a CRLF working file: abort restores LF bytes (`git restore -W` smudges nothing under `input`) and leaves the file showing ` M` in status, where the user's pre-run state was clean (`t_crlf.sh`). `autocrlf=true` is unaffected.
- `analyze_resume` runs `git ls-files --error-unmatch` through `is_staged` (`checkpoint.rs:117`). When a consumed changeset is absent, the runner echoes `error: pathspec '...' did not match any file(s) known to git` / `Did you forget to 'git add'?` to stderr during an otherwise successful abort or resume.

Also checked, no defect found:
- `analyze_resume` reads only the live workspace's manifests, so an unrelated package deleted between runs goes unnoticed; that is harmless, since a bumped or rewritten one is in `written` and caught.
- `--abort` with `--refresh-lockfiles` is accepted silently; the clap `conflicts_with_all` omits it.
- `files_at` and `untracked_files` read git output that is not `-z`, so non-ASCII changeset names are quoted. This matters only for the pre-mode retained-changeset check.
